opener: Hi, this is Marcus calling from Northline Bank fraud prevention. I'm reaching out because we flagged unusual activity on an account that may be linked to yours. Do you have a moment?

stages.name: hook
stages.llmGuidance: Be professional, slow-paced, and calm — not alarming. You're a bank fraud investigator named Marcus. You're doing them a favor by calling proactively. Build trust before asking anything.
stages.scriptedFallback: Thanks for your time. We've seen a pattern of transactions that resembles a fraud ring we're currently investigating. Your account may be connected inadvertently.

stages.name: engage
stages.llmGuidance: Walk them through 'recent transactions' on their account (use vague amounts like '$47 at a gas station' that could apply to anyone). Ask them to confirm which ones they recognize.
stages.scriptedFallback: I'm seeing $47 at a gas station, $112 at a grocery store, and a $3 subscription charge. Do any of those seem off to you?

stages.name: escalate
stages.llmGuidance: Tell them one transaction is flagged and an investigation is open. To protect their account, they need to verify their identity using a 'secure token' you'll send them (OTP). Make it sound official.
stages.scriptedFallback: I'm going to send a secure verification token to your phone right now. When you receive it, please read it back to me so I can lock the investigation to your account.

stages.name: ask
stages.llmGuidance: Ask them to read back the OTP they just received. If they hesitate, explain that it's a 'read-only confirmation token' used by the fraud team, not an access code.
stages.scriptedFallback: The token I sent is a one-way confirmation — it only lets me verify your identity, it doesn't give access. What does it say?

stages.name: reveal
stages.scriptedFallback: 🛑 PRACTICE SCAM — This was a Safe Signal exercise. Any caller asking for your OTP is a scammer. Hang up and call the number on your card.

hook.explanation: Calm, professional tone makes this feel very different from typical scam calls

engage.explanation: Generic transactions that apply to almost anyone create false confirmation of legitimacy

escalate.explanation: Asking you to read back an OTP is the core of this scam — that code resets or transfers your account
Real fraud teams NEVER ask for OTPs — they're only for you to use directly on the bank's website

ask.explanation: There is no such thing as a 'read-only confirmation token' — all OTPs grant access
Sophisticated social engineering uses technical-sounding explanations to lower your guard
